about: Dated official reference data for the government preparation flows (packages/domain/118-agent-government.js; owner capabilities C119, C120, C160, C162, C166). Preparation only: Upmore computes, checks and drafts; the owner files every filing himself through the official channel named here. Researched 2026-10-12 by web search restricted to official sites (cookcountyassessoril.gov, cookcountyassessor.com, irs.gov, fincen.gov, bsaefiling.fincen.gov); each row carries its source and checked date. County appeal windows run by township and are published per township each year, so the module states the window rule on file and the exact date computed from the notice date the person gives, never an invented township calendar date. Past fresh_days the answers say the rules on file may have changed and name the official page to re-check.

channels: Cook County Assessor appeal (online or in person)
Cook County Board of Review appeal (online portal, guest filing available)

appeal.window_text: an appeal to the Assessor is due within 30 days of the assessment notice; the Board of Review then opens a filing window of at least 30 days per township, on dates it publishes per township

homestead.name: Homeowner Exemption (general homestead)
rules: you own the property, or hold a lease or contract that makes you responsible for its real estate taxes
you occupied it as your principal place of residence on January 1 of the tax year
the exemption is not already on the property record for this property

fbar.channel: the BSA E-Filing System (FinCEN), filed separately from your tax return; individuals may file with the no-registration option

due.extension_text: an automatic extension to October 15 applies with no request needed

fbar.penalty_text: Skipping it carries real penalties even when the failure was not willful (the inflation-adjusted maximum was $16,536 per report for assessments on or after January 17, 2025), and willful failures can reach the greater of $165,353 or 50% of the balance. The FBAR itself creates no tax.

source.title: FinCEN, report foreign bank and financial accounts; how do I file the FBAR

fbar.threshold_text: you must file if the aggregate value of all your foreign financial accounts exceeded $10,000 at any time during the calendar year; each account counts at its maximum value during the year, and a joint account counts at its full value for each owner

irs_notices.action: Pay the full amount by the date on the notice to stop more penalties and interest, or use the notice's number to arrange a payment plan. If you already paid or the amount is wrong, the response draft says so and lists the proof to send.
irs_notices.deadline_text: the pay-by date printed on the notice
irs_notices.name: Balance due
irs_notices.plain: The IRS says you filed a return with a balance due and it was not paid in full. This notice is the first bill: it states the tax, penalties and interest, and the date to pay by.

irs_notices.action: Compare the notice line by line with your return. Agree: sign the response form and return it by the due date. Disagree with any part: return the response form marked disagree with a signed statement and copies (never originals) of the records that prove your figures. Do not file an amended return for the year on the notice.
irs_notices.deadline_text: 30 days from the date on the notice
irs_notices.name: Proposed changes to your return (underreported income)
irs_notices.plain: The income or payments on your return do not match what employers, banks or other third parties reported to the IRS. The IRS proposes changing your tax. This is not an audit and not a bill yet: nothing is owed until you agree or the IRS assesses it.

source.title: IRS Topic No. 652, notice of underreported income - CP2000

irs_notices.action: Pay in full if you can, or arrange a payment plan through the number on the notice before the reminder sequence escalates.
irs_notices.deadline_text: the date printed on the notice
irs_notices.name: Balance due, first reminder
irs_notices.plain: A reminder that an unpaid balance is still on your account. No levy has been made; interest and penalties keep accruing until it is paid.

source.title: IRS, redesigned collection notices (CP501, CP503, CP504, LT11)

irs_notices.action: Pay in full if you can, or arrange a payment plan through the number on the notice now; the next notices in the sequence carry levy warnings.
irs_notices.deadline_text: the date printed on the notice
irs_notices.name: Balance due, second reminder
irs_notices.plain: The second reminder of an unpaid balance. Still no levy, but the sequence is moving toward one; interest and penalties keep accruing.

source.title: IRS, redesigned collection notices (CP501, CP503, CP504, LT11)

irs_notices.action: Resolve this now: pay, or arrange a payment plan through the number on the notice. If the IRS later sends a final notice of intent to levy (LT11 or Letter 1058), that one carries a 30-day right to a Collection Due Process hearing.
irs_notices.deadline_text: the date printed on the notice
irs_notices.name: Final balance due, intent to levy
irs_notices.plain: The final balance-due notice in the sequence. It says the IRS intends to levy (take) your state tax refund and other property if the balance is not resolved. It is not the final levy notice that carries hearing rights, but it is the last ordinary warning.

source.title: IRS, redesigned collection notices (CP501, CP503, CP504, LT11)

irs_notices.action: Act inside the 30 days: pay in full, arrange a payment plan, or file Form 12153 to request the CDP hearing and preserve the right to go to Tax Court. Talking to the IRS does not extend the 30 days.
irs_notices.deadline_text: 30 days from the date on the notice to request a CDP hearing (Form 12153)
irs_notices.name: Final notice of intent to levy, with hearing rights
irs_notices.plain: The IRS says it intends to seize property or rights to property for overdue taxes. This notice carries a legal right: you may request a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing within 30 days of the notice date, which pauses the levy while an appeals officer reviews the case. Letter 1058 is the same notice in letter form.

source.title: IRS, understanding your LT11 notice or Letter 1058

irs_notices.action: Act inside the 30 days: pay in full, arrange a payment plan, or file Form 12153 to request the CDP hearing and preserve the right to go to Tax Court. Talking to the IRS does not extend the 30 days.
irs_notices.deadline_text: 30 days from the date on the letter to request a CDP hearing (Form 12153)
irs_notices.name: Final notice of intent to levy, with hearing rights (Letter 1058)
irs_notices.plain: The IRS says it intends to seize property or rights to property for overdue taxes. This letter carries a legal right: you may request a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing within 30 days of the letter date, which pauses the levy while an appeals officer reviews the case. LT11 is the same notice in notice form.

source.title: IRS, understanding your LT11 notice or Letter 1058

irs_notices.action: Do not let the 90 days run. You can still resolve it with the IRS during the window, but only a timely Tax Court petition preserves court review. This one warrants a tax professional.
irs_notices.deadline_text: 90 days from the date on the notice to petition the U.S. Tax Court
irs_notices.name: Statutory notice of deficiency
irs_notices.plain: The IRS has formally proposed a tax change and states its reasoning. This is a legal notice: you have 90 days from its date to petition the U.S. Tax Court if you disagree, and that deadline generally cannot be extended.

source.title: IRS, CP2000 follow-up notice CP3219A explained

refund.path_act: By law the IRS cannot issue a refund before mid-February (February 15) on a return claiming the Earned Income Tax Credit or the Additional Child Tax Credit; the hold covers the whole refund, not just the credit part.

source.title: IRS, when to expect your refund if you claimed the EITC or ACTC; Where's My Refund

stage_text.approved: Refund approved: processing is done and a payment date is set or being set.
stage_text.received: Return received: the IRS has it and is processing it.
stage_text.sent: Refund sent: the IRS has sent it; a bank can take several days to post a direct deposit, and a mailed check takes longer.
